title: Dispositions, Transfers & Callbacks
summary: Code every call correctly, complete cold transfers, and run the 3 scheduled callback process.

blocks.html: A disposition is the code you give a call when it ends. Accurate codes matter. Patterns of miscoding are improper call handling.

• Answering Machine: voicemail, ringing with no answer, or someone else answers and says they're not there. Example: "She's at work, try later."
  • Dead Air: you call their name twice at the start but get no response. Example: "Hello, Mary? ... Mary?" Nothing.
  • Not Interested (NI): they acknowledge you when you greet them but hang up at any point after. Example: they say "yeah?" then hang up during the opening.
  • Hung-Up Transfer: they hang up during or after starting the transfer process. Example: they hang up while it's ringing.
  • Robo: a fake automated voice, not a real person.
  • Transfer: the lead and agent connect and speak. Cold transfer completed.
  • Wrong Number: the person says you have the wrong number.
  • No English: the caller can't speak English.
  • DNC (Do Not Call): they tell you not to call in any way, use profanity, or threaten you. Try to read the DNC script if possible.
  • DQ (Disqualified): no Medicare Parts A and B; military coverage (VA, Tricare, Tricare for Life, CHAMPVA); insurance through work or retirement; covered by a Native American tribe.
  • Conference Ended: every transfer attempt ends with the agent's line disconnecting, a busy signal, or number-not-in-service.
  • No Agent: 5 transfer attempts, waiting at least 20 seconds each, and you still can't reach an agent.

blocks.question: You say "Hello, Robert?" twice and hear nothing. What is the disposition?
blocks.explanation: Calling their name twice with no response is Dead Air.

blocks.question: The consumer says "Hello?" then hangs up during your opening. What is the disposition?
blocks.explanation: They acknowledged you, then hung up. That's NI.

blocks.html:
These are the codes new fronters mix up most:

  • NI vs DQ: NI means they won't continue. DQ means they can't qualify.
  • NI vs Hung-Up Transfer: if they hang up before the transfer process starts, it's NI. During or after starting the transfer, it's Hung-Up Transfer.
  • NI vs DNC: "not interested, bye" is NI. "Stop calling me" is DNC.
  • Conference Ended vs No Agent: Conference Ended is when every attempt ends with the agent's line disconnecting, a busy signal, or number-not-in-service. No Agent is when you make 5 attempts, wait at least 20 seconds each, and nobody picks up.

blocks.question: You start the transfer and the consumer hangs up while it rings. What is the disposition?
blocks.explanation: Hanging up during or after starting the transfer is Hung-Up Transfer.

blocks.question: Every transfer attempt gives you a busy signal. What is the disposition?
blocks.explanation: Busy signal, disconnect, or not-in-service on every attempt is Conference Ended.

blocks.question: You make 5 transfer attempts, waiting 20+ seconds each, and no agent ever picks up. What happens?
choices: You can't reach an agent, so you follow the No Agent callback process
blocks.explanation: 5 attempts at 20+ seconds with no agent is No Agent territory. On the first call you schedule a callback.

blocks.question: The consumer answers "Yeah?" and then hangs up while you're asking the Medicaid question. What is the disposition?
blocks.explanation: They acknowledged you and hung up before the transfer process started. That's Not Interested.

lessons.title: The Cold Transfer Step by Step

blocks.html:
1. Get the verbal yes on "Give them JUST a few minutes to go over them with you, okay?" No yes, no transfer.
  2. Read the ringing line and press the transfer button.
  3. Fluff away while it rings.
  4. When the agent picks up, stop talking. Stay silent.
  5. The agent usually asks who they're speaking with. Wait until both parties speak.
  6. Press Leave Conference Call.
  7. Disposition as Transfer.

blocks.title: Don't leave too early
blocks.html: If you leave before you hear both the agent and the consumer speak, the call may not connect properly. Wait for both voices.

blocks.question: When do you press Leave Conference Call?
choices: Once you've heard both the agent and the consumer speak
As soon as it starts ringing
Right after the agent picks up, before anyone speaks
blocks.explanation: Wait for both parties to speak, then leave the conference and code Transfer.

blocks.html:
When you can't reach an agent, you don't give up on a qualified consumer. You follow the 3 scheduled callback rule:

  1. Initial call: 5 transfer attempts, at least 20 seconds each. If you can't reach an agent, schedule a callback at least 15 minutes out.
  2. First scheduled callback: do a full reconfirmation (the whole script again) and 5 attempts at 20 seconds. If the lead doesn't pick up, schedule the 2nd callback at least 15 minutes out. That still counts as an attempt.
  3. Second scheduled callback: same rules. Schedule the 3rd and final callback at least 15 minutes out.
  4. Third and final callback: same rules. If there's still no pickup or no agent, code as No Agent.

blocks.title: When callbacks stop
blocks.html: If the lead hangs up or DNCs you at any point, the callbacks stop. Code the call to match what happened.

After you complete the process, post in chat using this exact format, with the lead's number in front:

12345678910 NA CBS DONE

blocks.question: How far out must each scheduled callback be?
blocks.explanation: Every callback is scheduled at least 15 minutes out.

blocks.question: On a scheduled callback the lead answers. What do you do before transferring?
choices: A full reconfirmation of every question
Skip the questions since they already qualified

blocks.question: On the second callback, the lead says "Stop calling me." What happens?
choices: Read the DNC disclaimer, code DNC, and the callbacks stop
Rebut and try the transfer again
blocks.explanation: If the lead DNCs you, callbacks stop and you code accordingly.

questions.question: Someone answers and says "He's not here right now." What is the disposition?
questions.explanation: Someone else answering and saying they're not there is coded Answering Machine.

questions.question: A recorded automated voice picks up and starts a message. It's not a person. What is the disposition?
questions.explanation: A fake automated voice is Robo.

questions.question: When is a call coded Transfer?
choices: When you press the transfer button
When the lead and agent connect and speak
questions.explanation: Transfer means the cold transfer is completed: both parties connect and speak.

questions.question: A consumer says "You've got the wrong number, no one by that name lives here." What is the disposition?
questions.explanation: The person says you have the wrong number.

questions.question: How many transfer attempts, and how long each, before it counts as No Agent?
Every transfer attempt says the number is not in service. What is the disposition?
questions.explanation: Not-in-service on every attempt is Conference Ended.

questions.question: How many scheduled callbacks are in the no agent process?
questions.explanation: There are 3 scheduled callbacks. After the third, code No Agent.

questions.question: What is the chat post format after completing the callback process?
questions.explanation: Post the lead's number followed by NA CBS DONE.

questions.question: On the third and final callback there's still no agent. What do you code?
questions.explanation: Third callback, still no pickup or no agent: code No Agent.

questions.question: A consumer curses at you and threatens you. What is the disposition?
questions.explanation: The threat makes it DNC. Read the DNC script if possible. Swearing by itself is NOT a DNC. That's an objection you rebut.

questions.question: A consumer only speaks Spanish and you can't communicate. What is the disposition?
questions.explanation: A caller who can't speak English is No English.

questions.question: On a scheduled callback the lead doesn't pick up. What do you do (if it's not the final callback)?
choices: Stop the process and code NI
Schedule the next callback at least 15 minutes out; it still counts as an attempt
questions.explanation: No pickup still counts as an attempt; schedule the next callback 15+ minutes out.
